meta.title: Older-adult renter households for CHFA's older-adult capture rate
meta.method: Qualified older-adult renters for a unit = sum over CHAS income tiers of (tract CHAS elderly renter households in the tier) x (share of PUMS one- and two-person renter households with a householder 62 or older, in the tier, in the tract's PUMA, whose income is between the 40%-of-income rent floor and the AMI limit).
meta.rules_source: CHFA Housing Tax Credit Qualified Allocation Plan 2027-2028 (adopted 25 September 2026, approved by the Governor 23 October 2026), Appendix A Market Study Guide: "Older Adult, New Construction and Acquisition/Rehabilitation" (printed page 85) and the Older Adult Independent Living demand table (page 87)
rules: Renter households with a householder 62 or older (CHFA, page 85).
Rent no more than 40 percent of income (page 85).
One- or two-bedroom units with no more than two occupants; one- and two-person older-adult households (pages 85, 87).
Compared with existing age-restricted tax credit homes only; project-based Section 8 and assisted living left out (page 85).
In-migration only when demonstrated from comparable projects, with supporting information (page 86).
meta.reading: CHFA defines older-adult projects as "over the age of 55 or 62" (page 3) but names only a 62+ householder count for demand; a 55+ project is counted the same way here. That is COHO's reading, not a quoted rule.

chas.name: HUD CHAS 2018-2022, Table 7, renter households of the elderly family and elderly non-family types by HAMFI tier

pums.name: Census ACS 2020-2024 5-year PUMS, Colorado housing file (HHLDRAGEP 62+, NP 1-2, TEN 3 or 4)

limits_for_pums.name: CHFA 2024 income limits (50% AMI by household size), matching the 2024 dollars of PUMS incomes

meta.chas_types: CHAS "elderly family" = two persons, either or both 62 or over; "elderly non-family" = a householder 62 or over, alone or with non-relatives. In a few elderly-family households the householder is under 62.
meta.tract_layout: tracts[geoid] = [puma, lte30, 31to50, 51to80, 81to100, 100plus]; tracts_moe[geoid] = 90% margins, same tiers
meta.pums_layout: pumas[puma][size 1..6+][bin]; only sizes 1 and 2 are filled; bin i = income i% to i+1% of the size-adjusted AMI; last bin above 120%
meta.limitations: PUMS gives the income mix of older renters only by PUMA, so tracts in a PUMA share it; CHAS tract counts carry wide margins (tracts_moe). CHAS is 2018-2022; PUMS is 2020-2024.

two_person_split.layout: pumas[puma] = [share used, sample households, weight on the PUMA's own share, the PUMA's own share]; share used = weight * own + (1 - weight) * statewide, weight = n / (n + prior_cases)
two_person_split.source: Census ACS 2020-2024 5-year PUMS, Colorado housing file: renter households (TEN 3 or 4) of two people with income 20-60% of the size-adjusted AMI (CHFA 2024 limits), by bedrooms (BDSP)
